Rep. Valadao’s Health Care Workforce Innovation Act (H.R.7307) claims to address rural healthcare shortages by funneling grants to allied health training programs. But let’s be real—D.C. insiders will siphon these funds into bureaucratic slush funds while rural clinics still struggle. Section 2’s grant program sounds noble, but history shows these taxpayer-funded initiatives often enrich consultants and lobbyists instead of delivering real care. Trump’s America-First vision demands accountability, not more handouts to the same failed system. Cut the red tape and let states lead healthcare innovation—not federal bureaucrats.

Medicaid’s core mission is vital, but let’s be real—throwing more money at bloated bureaucracies isn’t the answer. HHS spending ballooned 51.7% from $1.2T to $1.7T since 2019, yet families still battle mold and asthma triggers in Central Valley homes. The problem isn’t funding—it’s systemic waste.

Medi-Cal’s own audits show billions vanish into administrative bloat instead of frontline care. Real support means slashing red tape, not rubber-stamping failed models.

Redirect that cash to secure borders, medical innovation, and direct aid—not middlemen.

Thank you Representative Valadao for recognizing the importance Medicaid to rural communities. 
Without access to appropriate services, care defaults to high-cost crisis and emergency departments and other sectors. More in our “Fact Sheet: Cuts to Behavioral Health Increase Costs to Californians.”

Medicaid’s role in rural areas isn’t about funding—it’s about bureaucratic bloat. Central Valley families deserve care, but throwing cash at a broken system won’t fix it. Look at the numbers: administrative costs eat up 15% of Medicaid budgets, while fraud drains billions.

Real reform means slashing red tape, cutting overpriced contracts, and redirecting funds to actual care—not expanding a program that rewards inefficiency. Rural hospitals need streamlined regulations and market-driven solutions, not more dependency on a bloated federal pipeline.

Let’s prioritize patients over paperwork.

The STOP Health Threats Act sounds noble until you realize it’s another Band-Aid on a bullet wound. The Reedley bio lab fiasco—where a code enforcement officer stumbled upon an illegal facility packed with COVID-19 and HIV strains—exposes the real issue: systemic failure to prioritize existing resources.

HHS and SSA top the efficiency leaderboard with $160B saved by axing waste like the $2.9B Office of Refugee Resettlement contract. Instead of dumping more cash into “training,” why not redirect the $1.9B Treasury blew on enterprise services or the $877M in HHS grants to states that clearly didn’t track outcomes?

Local cops shouldn’t need federal handouts to do basic inspections—they need D.C. to stop burning taxpayer money on slush funds and actually secure the homeland.

This bipartisan bill takes important steps to help officers recognize dangerous situations—like the illegal Reedley lab—before they put their lives at risk. I'm proud to help lead the fight to strengthen public safety and protect our families.

The Transgender Health Care Access Act (H.R. 2487) allocates $45M+ to expand gender-affirming care programs at community health centers (Sections 5-8). While CHCs serve vital roles in underserved areas, this bill prioritizes niche ideological initiatives over core medical needs. Taxpayers shouldn’t fund $15M for “gender-affirming care training” (Sec. 6) when rural clinics struggle with basic staffing.

Redirect that cash to maternal health, addiction treatment, or emergency services—not political pet projects. Valadao’s resolution ignores the fiscal insanity of tying CHC funding to progressive activism.

Fund healthcare, not bureaucracy.

This week is an important reminder of the life-saving work CHCs do every day, and I’m proud to join my colleagues in celebrating their impact.

The Enhanced Premium Tax Credit extension is just another DC band-aid on a bullet wound. While Valadao pretends to care about costs, the real issue is Medicaid collapse from bureaucratic bloat and millions added illegally to the rolls.

S.2073’s “State Public Option Act” proves the game: expand a broken system instead of fixing it. Every dollar spent on subsidies for non-citizens or administrative waste steals resources from veterans and working Americans.

Cut the fraud first—then talk about premiums.

By introducing a clean, one-year extension for the Enhanced Premium Tax Credit, we can protect families from these higher costs while Congress works toward a more permanent solution.
